text:
julia: heads-up — hitting sustained VRAM growth + page-table fragmentation on a long-context repro. started after the paged-attn kernel selection changes. repro is small but consistent on MI250x; H100 shows similar drift but less aggressive.
julia: repro command: `./repro_kvcache_longctx.sh --model paged-attn --seq 32768 --batch 8 --iters 1200 --warm 200`
julia: sympt: resident vram climbs linearly over time, kvcache page_table entries increase (not reclaimed), and later we see long pagewalk spikes (~10-50ms) per request. below is tail of trace:```
[172s] kvcache: alloc_page id=0x7f9c size=2MB owner=worker-3
[320s] kvcache: pt_remap migrate id=0x7f9c -> gpu1 (shadowflip=1)
[640s] kvcache: pagewalk_ms=12.3 (p99 48.7) kv_reuse_rate=0.72 pt_entries=134217
[900s] kvcache: pagewalk_ms=18.6 (p99 112.2) kv_reuse_rate=0.59 pt_entries=174321
[1180s] kvcache: mem_resident_mb=32456 vram_peak_mb=32768
```
julia: notes: when I force single-GPU (no migration) the growth stops. when I disable paged-attn (non-paged KV) the growth doesn't reproduce. implies bug in pager + pt remap path.
perf-bot: uploaded perf traces: https://perf.corp/redwood/trace/1732509876 (nvprof + perf + pprof). also attached a short flame showing a hotspot in `kv_pagewalk_coalesce` and repeated `pt_shadow_clone`.
yang: could be remap atomicity with the shadow page-table. if a remap can race with reuse/coalesce, we might be leaving tombstones that look like live entries to the reclamation pass.
yang: quick sanity check: can you dump pt_shadow flags around remap? i.e., enable `kvcache.debug=pt_trace` and grep for `shadowflip=1` events + their completion markers.
julia: done — trace shows many `shadowflip=1` w/o subsequent `shadow_commit` ~ 1 in 30 flips. those incomplete flips correlate with pt_entries bumps.
matt: h100 vs mi diff might be reorderings on the interconnect (nvlink vs infinity fabric) + kernel scheduling latency. the remap path uses an async fence; if fence isn't observed in the same ordering across archs you'll see stale owners.
matt: temporary mitigation: throttle migrations (set `pager.migration_concurrency=1`) and bump the reclaim scan frequency (`reclaim.scan_ms=50`). can you try?
julia: tried concurrency=1 — reduces slope but doesn't eliminate. reclaim.scan to 50ms spikes CPU but helps some. still leaves a slow leak.
nina: can you post the small repro binary? i'll run under valgrind-ish tracer and check for missing refcount clears on pt entries. also cc @yang for ordering tests.
julia: upload link: `s3://redwood-temp/kvcache/repro_1732509876.tar.gz` (small docker, model weights stubbed).
perf-bot: collected heap snapshots at 200s intervals: https://perf.corp/redwood/heapshots/1732509876.zip
yang: looking at flame + heapshots — evidence of fragments: many small page fragments (~64KB) that are never coalesced back into 2MB slabs. coalesce path seems to bail if `pt_owner != expected` which can happen if remap races.
yang: hypothesis: remap uses `pt_owner CAS` to flip ownership, but there is a window where the reuse bitmap still points to old subpages. if the coalesce path checks ownership before grabbing page locks, it skips, leaving the subpages orphaned.
matt: that fits with the `shadow_commit` missing events. win: we can add a small ordering fix: after CAS-ownership, issue `fence()` + check/clear reuse bitmap under lock. cheap patch to try.
julia: i'm going to build a branch with the extra `fence()` + guarded bitmap clear and run 2x long runs on MI250/H100. i'll post results here EOD.
nina: also add a quick unit test that simulates interleaved remap + coalesce (spawn two threads racing CAS + reclaim). will help CI catch regressions.
yang: if patch helps, we should still consider a longer-term fix: move to versioned page-table entries (epoch tags) so reclaim can check epochs instead of brittle ownership checks.
julia: plan: 1) run patched run and heap snapshots on both arches; 2) add unit repro in repo; 3) if green, ship as hotfix behind `pager.strict_ordering` flag.
matt: agreed. please add the test and tag me + eng-oncall if you flip the flag in prod.
julia: thanks. assigning myself: `KVCACHE-1427` (WIP). will update by 1732517000. :eyes:
